newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Mergers highlight options trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Mergers highlight options trade.

text.p: A few big mergers announced Tuesday highlighted options trading as investors sought to take advantage of sharp price moves and arbitrage opportunities, traders said.
Among the most active were options on shares of H.F. Ahmanson and Co, which early Tuesday offered to buy Great Western Financial Corp for $42.53 per share, or a total of $6 billion.
Ahmanson shares were up four at 44-1/2 in late session trading. Consolidated volume neared four million shares.
Most of the Ahmanson action was in the calls, led by the March 40 with volume of 4,025 contracts. Its open interest was 77, which included an addition of seven contracts last Friday.
The March 42-1/2, a new listing, traded about 2,735 contracts and the April 42-1/2, also new, traded nearly 1,400.
Great Western shares surged 10-3/4 to 45 on consolidated volume of about 9.2 million shares.
Activity in Great Western options was also focused on the calls, where the July 35, with volume of 1,260, was most active. Its open interest was 1,743, with 31 contracts closed last Friday.
One trader said public investors were big holders of the Great Western July 30 and 35 calls and had sold those out in morning trading.
"The public open interest is done and now it's just professionals and arbs starting to figure things out," he said, adding that most trading was being done in relatively small blocks.
Forty and 45 strike prices were added.
In the healthcare sector, Healthsouth Corp said it would buy Horizon/CMS Healthcare Corp in a stock swap valued at $1.6 billion, including about $700 million in debt.
Under the deal, HealthSouth would exchange 0.42169 of its shares for each Horizon share.
"Mostly people are trying to put on the arbitrage between the two stocks," an options trader in New York said, adding that they were trying to sell Healthsouth and buy Horizon.

"What they're doing is selling the deep (in-the-money) calls," he said. "Firms that have customers that want to sell the deep calls will buy the calls from them, exercise the calls and immediately sell the stock."
Thus the heaviest trading in HealthSouth options was in the February 30 calls, with volume of nearly 2,700 contracts.
The trader in New York said most of the other volume was two-way trade.
HealthSouth shares lost 2-1/8 to 41 and Horizon gained 2-1/4 to 16-1/2.
The Horizon February 10 calls were most active, with total volume of 1,950 contracts.
Elsewhere, Marriott International Inc offered to buy Renaissance Hotel Group NV for $30 cash per share in a deal valued at $1 billion including debt.
Marriott options were not particularly active. No options are listed on Renaissance. ((--G.Crawford, 312 408 8750/Email: derivatives@reuters.com))
